messages.author: d6d83e22ef3ba9f1
messages.subject: Re: lavaan WARNING: some estimated ov variances are negative
parts:
Hi Heather, 

Below is the code I used to troubleshoot what is going on in this case. The issue is that the IBD variable is estimated to have a negative residual variance, but this can easily be fixed with a model constraint (also in the code below). The reason for the negative residual is likely that IBD has a generally larger genetic correlation with your other variables, so the technically best fitting parameters explain > 1 standardized variance in IBD. To be honest, I'm not sure why you are getting the mclapply error messages for addSNPs (this would be a separate issue from the negative residual variance message); is this something you ran into for other runs of addSNPs? At any rate, the code below should fix the negative residual issue. 

Best, 
  Andrew 


#load in LDSC object
load("LDSCoutput_autoinf.RData")

#IBD estimated with negative residual variance 
#outside of multivariate GWAS context.
commonfactor(LDSCoutput_autoinf)

#examine average genetic correlation for each variable. IBD is paritcularly high
colMeans(cov2cor(LDSCoutput_autoinf$S))

#fix IBD residual to be above 0
model<-"F1=~CRO+UC+IBD+PSC+MS
IBD~~a*IBD
a > .001"

#confirm this works with usermodel
usermodel(LDSCoutput_autoinf,model=model)

#specify model for userGWAS
model<-"F1=~CRO+UC+IBD+PSC+MS
F1~SNP
IBD~~a*IBD
a > .001"

##run userGWAS in parallel (after running addSNPs). Save only F1~SNP for memory reasons
results<-userGWASpar(Output,estimation="DWLS", model=model,sub=c("F1~SNP"))
